concepts.def: Mid-1940s US movement of large gestural abstracts.
Experimental work ahead of its time.

walkthroughs.body_html: Cubism was founded by Picasso and Braque around 1907 and developed until 1914. They broke objects into geometric facets and showed several viewpoints at once. Analytical Cubism is monochrome and complex; Synthetic Cubism adds collage.

Founded by André Breton in 1924, Surrealism drew on Freud's ideas of the unconscious. Dalí painted melting clocks; Magritte painted pipes that were not pipes. Automatism let artists draw without planning to bypass logic.

In 1940s New York, Abstract Expressionism shifted attention from subject to the act of painting itself. Jackson Pollock's drip paintings are pure action painting; Rothko's huge colour fields aim at meditative emotion.
